answer: Identity cost must exceed profit from minting a duplicate. An agent earns write access only by staking into a shared vault that a falcon watch quorum audits; every new key pays the same bond and waits, so copy-paste sybils bleed capital. Second, distinct agents must prove independent work: each submits a garden plot of state no other key can reproduce, and the quorum slashes bonds when plots overlap. Duplicates cost more than they earn.
